name: ntopng
description: Imports the four hosts a real ntopng Community Edition built from traffic two containers actually generated and a third actually captured, and proves the two things no hand-written fixture would produce: the fe80:: rows ntopng files as LOCAL hosts are dropped, and active.lua really does omit totalRows so paging has to stop on a short page.
_image_note: THE ONE UNPINNED IMAGE IN THIS SUITE, by an explicit waiver of the pin-every-tag rule. `ntop/ntopng` publishes exactly one tag -- `latest` -- so there is no version to pin to; the stable channel has no arm64 build and no alternative repository either. The digest above is the image this case was actually written and verified against, recorded so that a future failure can be attributed to an upstream rebuild rather than to the integration. Re-record it after a deliberate upgrade: `docker inspect --format '{{index .RepoDigests 0}}' ntop/ntopng:latest`. The version that digest reports itself as is ntopng 6.6.260814 (6.6-stable, built 2026-08-14).
_ready_note: One gate, and it is deliberately the login page rather than a REST endpoint. Every REST v2 URL answers 302 until the seed retires the default password, so a REST gate would have to accept a redirect and would then be proving nothing. The seed does the real waiting: it polls the host table until the captured traffic has been parsed and reverse DNS has landed.
_kwargs_note: host_mode stays at its default of `local`. `all` would additionally return every remote peer the segment talked to, which on a real sensor is the public internet and is not inventory; here the compose network is isolated, so `all` would prove nothing that `local` does not. The token is generated by ntopng and discovered by the seed -- it cannot be hard-coded.

fields._match.behavior: no-id-match no-id-break mac-match mac-break ip-match ip-break name-match name-break

_expect_notes.link_local: The strongest assertion here, and entirely undesigned. The containers' own IPv6 stacks emit MLD and neighbour-solicitation traffic, and ntopng files each fe80:: address as a host with is_localhost true -- meaning `inside the local networks`, not loopback. The platform's IsUnicast deliberately KEEPS link-local, so these addresses would reach real assets if the integration did not filter them, and two unrelated hosts that both derived an fe80 address would then correlate to each other. The address is derived from a randomly generated veth MAC, so the seed discovers it and fails loudly if ntopng reported none -- otherwise this assertion would pass for the wrong reason.
_expect_notes.totalRows: The seed reports total_rows_present, and against this build it is false: active.lua's envelope carries only currentPage, perPage, data and sort. That is what the integration assumes when it stops paging on the first short page instead of counting towards a total, and it is now confirmed against the software rather than inferred from its source.
_expect_notes.os: os=5 is nDPI's ndpi_os enum for Linux, and ntopng really did fingerprint both busybox clients that way from their HTTP requests to the sniffer. The sniffer itself is os=0 -- it only ever answered, so there was nothing to fingerprint -- which is why `os` is asserted absent there. The enum mapping in the script is therefore exercised on a real value rather than a chosen one.
_expect_notes.client_b_mac: client-b is configured 02:42:0a:de:09:0b, the shape of every default Docker MAC. ntopng reports it verbatim as 02:42:0A:DE:09:0B -- which is also why ntopng_mac is asserted in upper case, since ntopng upper-cases hex -- and the platform's network_interface() clears the locally-administered bit, so macAddresses reads 00:42:0a:de:09:0b. Asserting both sides makes the transformation visible.
_expect_notes.hostnames: Discovered, not chosen. ntopng resolved the two running clients through Docker's embedded resolver, so their names carry the compose project name and therefore the harness pid. The sniffer container has already exited by then, so its PTR is gone and active.lua falls back to putting the host's own address in the `name` field -- exactly the case the integration's _hostname() rejects. That fallback is asserted directly: ntopng_name holds the IP, and hostnames is empty. The bridge gateway is the same case for a different reason: nothing ever published a name for it.
_expect_notes.gateway: Not seeded -- discovered. 10.222.9.1 is the compose bridge itself, and it is in the table because the sniffer pings it during the capture window. Its MAC is generated by Docker per network, so nothing about it is asserted beyond its identity and its lack of a hostname.
_expect_notes.services: ntopng observes flows, and a host that made an HTTP request is a client rather than a listener on 80. No Service is produced for any asset, which is asserted rather than assumed.
_expect_notes.deviceType_is_absent_on_purpose: ntopng labels an ordinary Linux container 'Networking' in its MAC table. That names a traffic role, not a chassis -- it cannot say switch vs router -- so DEVICE_TYPE_LABELS maps it to nothing and the asset carries no deviceType. The raw label is still asserted via ntopng_mac_device_type, so this proves BOTH halves: ntopng really did supply a device type, and the integration deliberately declined to translate it rather than guessing and overriding fingerprinting, which can tell those apart. If a future ntopng labels these hosts something mappable, deviceType appears and this expectation flips.

_findings.auth_failure_is_302_not_200: The integration's comment says an auth failure returns an HTML login page with HTTP 200 rather than a 401. The raw response is actually a 302 to /lua/login.lua; it becomes the HTML page with status 200 only after a redirect-following client follows it, which the runtime's HTTP client does. So the behaviour the integration handles is real and its handling is correct, but the underlying status is a redirect. Verified against this build with a deliberately wrong token: the run logs `listing interfaces: the response was not JSON, which is what ntopng returns when it redirects an unauthenticated request to the login page` and reports zero assets without aborting.
_findings.broadcast_mac_survives_the_filter: RESOLVED 2026-08-16. _real_mac compared the NORMALIZED value against its sentinel list, but normalize_mac clears the locally-administered bit, rewriting ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff to fd:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff so broadcast never matched and was emitted as a real MAC under a spelling no NIC has ever had. The all-zero address has that bit clear already, which is why only broadcast escaped. The filter now tests the raw hex. Regression-locked in ntopng/tests/fixtures/malformed.json, which indexes exactly 1 MAC from a 5-row table.
_findings.device_type_label_passes_through_verbati: RESOLVED 2026-08-16. The script now maps ntopng's device_type_label through DEVICE_TYPE_LABELS instead of passing it through. This mattered because runZero accepts a closed set of device types (IdentifyTypeFromCustomIntegration) and SILENTLY DISCARDS anything else -- no error, no log line -- so 'Workstation' and 'Networking' were thrown away at the far end while looking set. seed.py mirrors the same map so this manifest asserts the mapped value. Labels with no honest equivalent map to nothing: 'Networking' cannot say switch vs router, and a guess would override fingerprinting, which can tell them apart.
